payload.title: Name Change After Marriage Step by Step in Australia
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s with a budget of AUD 150k or more, planning or just back from a destination wedding, who want to know whether either of them needs to legally change a surname, which certificate the government will actually accept, the order to update their records in, and how it works when the marriage certificate was issued overseas, so the paperwork does not clash with passports and travel around the wedding.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor: request a Wedded Concierge consultation at /wonderland-concierge so an advisor can plan the venue, travel, vendors and guest stays for the celebration abroad (the name change, certificates and all legal paperwork stay with the couple and the official agencies).
payload.angle: Page-one results for 'name change after marriage' are mostly checklist blogs from private services, banks and wedding sites that blur the ceremonial certificate with the official one, quote fees and skip state differences, and none deal with a marriage certificate issued abroad. This guide answers the question only as official Australian sources state it, dated once as at November 2026: whether you need to legally change your name or can use your marriage certificate (credited to each state or territory BDM as sourced), getting the official registry certificate rather than the ceremonial one, then updating records in a sensible order using the Australian Passport Office, Services Australia, the ATO, the AEC and one state transport agency as an example (private bodies only as 'ask them'). It covers keeping your name or both partners changing as sourced, then the destination angle page one misses: using an overseas marriage certificate (translation, Apostille, and how each state treats it, as sourced), and timing the passport around wedding and honeymoon travel only as the Passport Office or Smartraveller says. Calm, exact and practical, with no legal advice.
must_include: Intro with a direct answer in the first 100 words: in Australia you generally update records using your official marriage certificate, and whether a formal change of name is needed depends on your state or territory and your situation, as each BDM states it, dated 'as at November 2026' [[VERIFY]]. Then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways (certificate versus formal change by state; use the official registry certificate, not the ceremonial one; update the passport and government records in order; an overseas certificate may need translation or an Apostille, as sourced).

Do you need to legally change your name: marriage certificate route versus a formal change of name registration, credited to each state or territory BDM as sourced (a table by state is welcome if every cell is sourced), with [[VERIFY]] markers until sourced. 'A fee may apply' only where a source says so; no amounts.

Get the right certificate: the official certificate issued by the state or territory registry versus the ceremonial certificate signed on the day, how to order it only as each BDM states, linking /expert-advice/notice-of-intended-marriage and /expert-advice/who-can-perform-a-marriage (drafts; link only if live at publish).

Step by step updating your records, in order, written as numbered steps: Australian Passport Office, Services Australia (Medicare and Centrelink as it states), the ATO, the AEC, one state transport agency as an example for the driver licence; then 'ask them' for banks, employers, insurers, utilities and other private bodies, with no names. Each step only as the agency states, with [[VERIFY]] until sourced.
Keeping your name, or both partners changing (including a double-barrelled or new surname, and a partner taking the other's name), only as official sources state; framed as a choice, not advice.

If you married overseas (the differentiator): using a foreign marriage certificate in Australia, translation requirements, the Apostille or other legalisation, and how each state or territory BDM treats an overseas marriage for a name change, all as sourced. Link /expert-advice/overseas-marriage-certificate, /expert-advice/do-you-have-to-register-an-overseas-marriage-at-home, /expert-advice/what-is-an-apostille-and-does-my-paperwork-need-one and /destination-weddings/is-marriage-in-italy-recognised-in-australia (draft; link only if live at publish), rather than restating them.

Travel timing: booking flights in the name on the current passport and when to update the passport around wedding and honeymoon travel, only as the Australian Passport Office or Smartraveller states. This section or the overseas section carries the ONLY Advisor line in the body, from brand-facts.md ('One Wedded Advisor, start to finish, as a single point of contact.' or equivalent brand-facts wording), tied to the celebration abroad, never paperwork, plus the /wonderland-concierge link (anchor 'Wedded Concierge').

FAQ (4 to 6): Do I have to change my name after marriage in Australia? Is my marriage certificate enough to change my name? Which certificate do I need? What order should I update my documents in? Can I change my name with an overseas marriage certificate? Should I travel on my old or new passport after the wedding? Each answer from the same sources as the body.

Close: the one Advisor line from brand-facts.md (never the Wedded Advisor definition line or its closing phrase). Links /wonderland-concierge (Wedded Concierge) and /magazine as the magnet. UTMs utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=name-change-after-marriage&utm_content=primary|secondary|magnet|closing on /wonderland-concierge and /magazine only.
avoid: Any legal or procedural statement not from an official Australian source (state and territory BDMs, Australian Passport Office, Services Australia, ATO, AEC, the chosen state transport agency, DFAT, Smartraveller) read live; undated claims; legal advice ('check with the agency' instead).
Presenting one state's rules as national; every state rule credited to that state.
Any price, fee or amount; 'a fee may apply' only where sourced; 'free'.
Bank, insurer, employer, vendor or private name-change service names; private bodies only as 'ask them'.
Rules for marrying in a specific foreign country beyond what an official source states; link out rather than restate.
'Best' or ranking language; transfers, drive or flight times.
Anything implying the Wedded Advisor or Wedded Concierge helps with the name change, certificates, translations, Apostilles, passports or any legal paperwork.

Wedded Privileges; Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md; more than one Advisor line in the body besides the close; the Advisor definition line and the phrase 'last dance'; 'Wonderland Concierge' as anchor text.
Restating overseas certificate, registration, Apostille or recognition detail that their own pages own.
Research talk in copy ('we could not confirm', 'according to our research'); per-line source credits; hedge stacking.
Competitor wedding sites, private name-change kits, bank blogs or Wikipedia as sources; competitor wording or images.
Clichés, exclamation marks, keywords pasted in headings, em dashes, US spelling.
